stem: A facility switches water sources. The new source has nearly the same pH as the old source but a higher EC. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The sources are chemically equivalent because their pH values are similar
The higher EC indicates a different dissolved-ion load, so source-water records should be reviewed before assuming the existing program will behave identically
The higher EC means irrigation volume must be reduced by the same percentage
The pH similarity proves alkalinity and ion composition are unchanged
rationale: Similar pH does not establish equivalent source-water chemistry. A higher EC indicates a changed ionic load and warrants comparison with prior source-water records before management changes are made.
